Thanks for the tag, Priyom. I reviewed the redlines and had a sync with engineering on Monday morning. Key takeaways:

- Subprocessor disclosure: we already maintain a public registry and can add a contractual commitment to "notify customers of material changes to the subprocessor list within 10 business days." Proposed tweak: limit to "material" changes or subprocessors that will process customer-produced data. This avoids noise for routine infra swaps (e.g., ephemeral monitoring agents).

- Retention (30-day max): engineering strongly prefers a 90-day default for request/response logs that include request identifiers to preserve troubleshooting and model quality monitoring. However, we can support a 30-day retention commitment for PII-containing logs if we can: (1) classify and route PII-bearing telemetry into a separate bucket, and (2) allow a security-forensics exception of up to 180 days with documented justification and audit trail.

Action items for the thread:
1) Laura / Hannah: confirm whether the forensics exception above is acceptable from a compliance standpoint and whether we need additional controls (e.g., extra encryption, HSM-wrapped keys, or MFA for access).
2) Priyom: propose the customer-facing language I should include in the counter-draft.

I'll draft suggested language for the subprocessor notification and a retention carve-out by EOD Tuesday.

– Soojin

Subject: RE: Acme DPA redlines (subprocessors + retention)

Marta / Priyom — thanks for patience while we evaluated. Summary of our position and proposed contract language below.

Summary: we can accept a contractual commitment to notify customers of material subprocessor additions within 10 business days where the subprocessor will have access to customer-generated data or PII. We cannot commit to notifying for every operational vendor change.

For retention: we cannot agree to a blanket 30-day maximum for all logs because it would impair incident response and model quality workflows. Proposed compromise:
- Redwood will retain telemetry logs that contain identifiers for up to 90 days by default.
- For telemetry that includes PII (as defined in Section X), Redwood will retain for up to 30 days unless Customer provides in writing a documented forensics justification. In such cases Redwood may retain the relevant PII-bearing logs for up to 180 days solely for investigation, with access limited to authorized security personnel and subject to audit logging.

Proposed contract snippets you can insert into the DPA redline: 
1) Subprocessor notification: "Redwood shall notify Customer of material additions to the list of subprocessors who will process Customer Data within ten (10) business days of Redwood becoming contractually bound to such subprocessor. 'Material' includes any subprocessor that will have access to Customer Data, PII, or ability to export Customer Data outside of the Customer's specified region."

2) Retention carve-out: "Redwood retains logs for service operation and security purposes. Telemetry containing PII will be deleted within thirty (30) days except where Customer furnishes a written request with a documented justification for an extended retention period for investigatory purposes. In those cases Redwood may retain specified telemetry for a period not to exceed one hundred eighty (180) days, and such retention shall be subject to access controls and audit logging as described in Annex 3."

If that language looks OK to Acme, we can produce a clean counter-draft and track the forensics exception with a narrow SLA and access controls. Priyom — recommend sending this to Marta with the redline PDF attached and the new snippets inline.

-Laura
